title: dembrane v3: what is going wrong
description: Only what is failing, everywhere: production, staging, the pull request previews and sam. The first row is the state right now, the second counts what went wrong in the selected time, then one row per layer with the detail. Zero and green mean nothing is wrong there. Log based panels read at most 13 hours.

panels.title: Alerts firing
panels.description: Alert rules that are true now. "posted to Slack" counts the critical and notice alerts: above zero, people are affected now or will be soon, and the table below says which. "warnings" are not posted: nobody is affected yet, something is drifting.

panels.title: Workers up
panels.description: Workers that are up, of the number that should run. They do the transcription, summaries, reports and emails. Orange when one is missing; red under half: that work is slow or stopped, while recording still works and the audio is kept.

targets.expr: (max(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="$namespace", deployment="dembrane-web-worker"}) / max(kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace="$namespace", deployment="dembrane-web-worker"})) * on () group_left (up) count_values("up", max(kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="$namespace", deployment="dembrane-web-worker"})) * on () group_left (wanted) count_values("wanted", max(kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace="$namespace", deployment="dembrane-web-worker"}))

panels.title: Workers alive
panels.description: The API is asked from outside whether a worker checked in during the last 90 seconds. NO: background work is not running, also when the workers look up.

panels.title: Reachable from outside
panels.description: The public addresses, asked from outside every 30 seconds: the app, the recording page for participants, the API, and the API's own check of its database. DOWN: people cannot use that part.

panels.title: Audio waiting
panels.description: Pieces of audio from the last hour that have no transcript and no error yet, counted in the database. A handful is normal while people record. A number that keeps climbing: transcription is behind and people see no text appear.

targets.rawSql: select chunks_waiting_1h as value from obs.live_now

panels.title: Longest wait for a worker
panels.description: How long the oldest job has waited for a worker. "transcription" is red from 2 minutes (the alert): people who record see no transcript appear. "other work" (summaries, reports, emails, analysis) is orange from 15 minutes (the alert): those arrive late. "no report": no worker wrote its queue numbers in the last 3 minutes, which also means the workers are not running.

panels.title: Alerts that are firing
panels.description: One line per alert that is true now, warnings included. Empty: nothing is firing. The Slack message of an alert says who feels it and the first step.

panels.title: When alerts were firing
panels.description: One bar per alert, drawn for as long as it was true. Red and orange bars were posted to Slack (critical, notice); grey bars are warnings. Empty: no alert fired in the selected time.

panels.title: In the selected time: what went wrong, layer by layer
Container restarts
panels.description: Times a program in the cluster stopped and was started again, and how many of those were for running out of memory. Each restart of an app service fails what it was doing: a request, or a job that then starts over.

targets.expr: sum((max by (namespace, pod, container) (max_over_time(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"}[$__range])) == 1) * on (namespace, pod, container) group_left () sum by (namespace, pod, container) (round(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[$__range])))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Requests to production that got a server error. Each one is a page that did not load or a change that was not saved for somebody.

targets.expr: sum(round(max by (controller_pod, ingress, host, status, method, path) (increase(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{namespace="$namespace", status=~"5.."}[$__range])))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Error lines
panels.description: Lines the production services wrote at error level. Each is something that failed for a request or a job; the tables below show which.

panels.title: Audio failures
panels.description: Times that transcribing a piece of audio, joining a recording or writing a summary failed. That piece or recording has no text or no summary unless a later try worked.

targets.rawSql: select coalesce(sum(n), 0) as value from obs.minute_pipeline where $__timeFilter(minute) and event like '%.failed'

panels.title: AI failures
panels.description: Calls to the AI model that ended in an error, or that the model refused to answer. The transcript, summary or chat answer that needed it is missing or late.

targets.rawSql: select count(*) as value from obs.model_calls where $__timeFilter(started_at) and (status <> 'ok' or finish_reason in ('safety', 'content-filter', 'recitation', 'blocklist', 'prohibited_content', 'spii'))

panels.title: Staging
panels.description: Requests to staging that got a server error, and lines its services and workers wrote at error level. No customer is affected; a change that is about to be released may be broken.

panels.title: PR previews
panels.description: Requests to the pull request previews that got a server error, and lines its services and workers wrote at error level. No customer is affected; a change that is about to be released may be broken.

panels.title: sam
panels.description: Requests to sam, the team's agent in Slack, that did not end the normal way: cut by a restart, ended in an error, got stuck or ran out of time. Someone may still be waiting for an answer.

targets.rawSql: select count(*) as value from obs.sam_sessions where $__timeFilter(started_at) and exit_state <> 'clean'

panels.title: Work that is stuck or failing (production)
Jobs waiting, by queue
panels.description: Jobs that are ready and that no worker has picked up, by queue. Only a queue with jobs waiting gets a line. The dashed line is the number of jobs being worked on: jobs waiting while nothing is worked on means the work is stuck. No line at all means no worker reports.

panels.title: Longest wait, by queue
panels.description: How long the oldest waiting job of each queue has waited. The dashed lines are the alerts: 2 minutes for transcription (conversations.chunk), 15 minutes for every other queue. Above them, what that queue makes arrives late.

panels.title: Audio received and not yet transcribed
panels.description: Pieces of audio received minus pieces transcribed, added up from the start of the selected time. A line that climbs: transcription is not keeping up and people see no text appear. It starts at zero whatever was waiting before, and a piece that failed stays counted.

targets.rawSql: select minute as time, sum(sum(received) - sum(done)) over (order by minute) as "not yet transcribed" from (select minute, chunks as received, 0 as done from obs.minute_chunks where $__timeFilter(minute) union all select minute, 0, n from obs.minute_pipeline where $__timeFilter(minute) and event = 'task_transcribe_chunk.completed') m group by minute order by minute

panels.title: Audio steps that failed
panels.description: Failed steps on the way from audio to text, by step: transcribing a piece, joining the pieces of a recording, writing the summary. That piece or recording has no text or summary unless a later try worked.

targets.rawSql: select $__timeGroupAlias(minute, 5m), replace(replace(replace(event, 'task_', ''), '.failed', ''), '_', ' ') as metric, sum(n) as value from obs.minute_pipeline where $__timeFilter(minute) and event like '%.failed' group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Jobs that failed, by job
panels.description: Tries of a background job that threw an error, by job. A failed try is run again; a job that keeps failing never delivers what it makes (an email, a webhook, a report).

targets.expr: sum by (job) (count_over_time({namespace="$namespace", component="worker"} |= "\"message\":\"job failed\"" | json job="job" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Jobs taken over after a worker died
panels.description: Jobs that were running on a worker that disappeared, and that another worker started again. Bars here mean workers are dying in the middle of their work; that work is late.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({namespace="$namespace", component="worker"} |= "resumed workflows of a dead worker" | json resumed="resumed" | __error__="" | unwrap resumed [$__interval]))

panels.title: Model calls that failed or were refused
panels.description: Calls to the AI model that ended in an error (by its name) or that the model refused (by its reason; safety is the model's own filter). The transcript, summary or answer that needed the call is missing or late.

targets.rawSql: select $__timeGroupAlias(started_at, 5m), case when status <> 'ok' then 'error: ' || coalesce(error, status) else 'refused: ' || finish_reason end as metric, count(*) as value from obs.model_calls where $__timeFilter(started_at) and (status <> 'ok' or finish_reason in ('safety', 'content-filter', 'recitation', 'blocklist', 'prohibited_content', 'spii')) group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Error lines, by service
panels.description: Lines written at error level, by service. Each is something that failed for a request or a job. No bars: there were none.

panels.title: Warning lines, by service
panels.description: Lines written at warning level, by service: something went wrong and the service carried on, for example a piece of audio that could not be transcribed. No bars: there were none.

panels.title: The same line, counted
panels.description: Every kind of error and warning line of the selected time, and how often it was written: the fastest way to see what is failing most. Fixed words only, nothing a person typed or said.

targets.expr: sum by (component, severity, signal, message) (count_over_time({namespace="$namespace"} |~ "\"severity\":\"(WARNING|ERROR|CRITICAL)\"" | json severity="severity", signal="signal", message="message" | __error__="" [$__range]))

panels.title: Newest error lines
panels.description: The newest 200 lines at error level, newest first: when, which service, what failed. Search the request id in the logs for everything else that happened in that request or job.

panels.title: Newest warning lines
panels.description: The newest 200 lines at warning level, newest first, with the same columns.

panels.title: Containers that restarted, and why
panels.description: Times a program stopped and was started again, by program and by the reason of its last stop. "ran out of memory": it used more memory than it is allowed. What it was doing failed or starts over.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, container, why) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace((max by (namespace, pod, container, reason) (max_over_time(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason[$__interval])) == 1) * on (namespace, pod, container) group_left () sum by (namespace, pod, container) (round(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[$__interval]))), "why", "$1", "reason", "(.*)"), "why", "ran out of memory", "reason", "OOMKilled"), "why", "stopped with an error", "reason", "Error"), "why", "ended by itself", "reason", "Completed")) > 0

panels.title: Which containers restarted
panels.description: One line per container that restarted in the selected time, with the reason of its last stop. Empty: nothing restarted.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, pod, container, why) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace((max by (namespace, pod, container, reason) (max_over_time(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason[$__range])) == 1) * on (namespace, pod, container) group_left () sum by (namespace, pod, container) (round(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[$__range]))), "why", "$1", "reason", "(.*)"), "why", "ran out of memory", "reason", "OOMKilled"), "why", "stopped with an error", "reason", "Error"), "why", "ended by itself", "reason", "Completed")) > 0

panels.title: Services short of instances
panels.description: Copies of a service that should run and do not, by service. One short: less room for a busy moment. A service whose every copy is missing is down for the people who use it.

panels.title: Pods that cannot start or are not ready
panels.description: Pods (the running copies of a service) that are stuck, by what holds them: one that keeps crashing and waits for its next try, one whose image cannot be fetched, one that waits for room on a machine, one that runs and fails its health check. A short bump during a release is normal; a line that stays means that service has fewer copies, or none.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, container, state) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(max by (namespace, pod, container, reason) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason!~"ContainerCreating|PodInitializing"}), "state", "$1", "reason", "(.*)"), "state", "keeps crashing, waits for its next try", "reason", "CrashLoopBackOff"), "state", "its image cannot be fetched", "reason", "ImagePullBackOff|ErrImagePull"), "state", "its configuration is not complete", "reason", "CreateContainerConfigError")) > 0

targets.legendFormat: {{namespace}}: waiting for room or to start

targets.expr: sum by (namespace) (max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_ready{condition="false"}) * on (namespace, pod) max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Running"})) > 0

panels.title: Memory used, as a share of the limit
panels.description: The fullest container of each production service, against the memory it is allowed. Dashed orange at 85 % is the alert; at 100 % (red) the container is stopped and restarts, and what it was doing fails. Containers outside production show only above 80 %.

targets.expr: max by (component) (label_replace(container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="$namespace", container!="", image!=""} / on (namespace, pod, container) group_left () max by (namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="$namespace", resource="memory"}), "component", "$1", "pod", "dembrane-web-([a-z]+)-.*"))

max by (namespace, container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace!="$namespace", container!="", image!=""} / on (namespace, pod, container) group_left () max by (namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace!="$namespace", resource="memory"})) > 0.8

panels.title: Requests that failed, by site
panels.description: Requests to production that got a server error, by site (the first part of the address) and error code. Each bar is people for whom a page did not load or a change was not saved.

targets.expr: sum by (site, status) (label_replace(round(max by (controller_pod, ingress, host, status, method, path) (increase(nginx_ingress_controller_requests{namespace="$namespace", status=~"5.."}[$__interval]))), "site", "$1", "host", "([^.]+).*")) > 0

panels.title: Machines in trouble
panels.description: The machines (nodes) the cluster runs on: how many are not ready, short of memory or short of disk. Above zero: the programs on that machine are moved or stopped, and services can lose copies.

panels.title: Cluster jobs that failed
panels.description: One-off jobs of the cluster (a migration before a release, the check after it, a scheduled report) that started in the selected time and failed. Empty: none failed. A failed migration means the release did not go out.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, job_name) (kube_job_status_start_time) * 1000 and on (namespace, job_name) (kube_job_status_failed > 0) and on (namespace, job_name) (kube_job_status_start_time > time() - $__range_s)

panels.title: Monitoring itself
panels.description: Whether this page and the alerts can be trusted. "alert rules checked" must say yes. The other three must be zero: alerts that could not be handed to the sender, rule checks that failed, and log lines that were dropped before they were stored, all in the selected time.

panels.title: What monitoring cannot reach
panels.description: Sources Prometheus asks for numbers and that do not answer, by group, with the size of the group. Panels that depend on such a source are empty or old. Empty: everything answers.

panels.title: Staging and PR previews (Google Cloud Run)
Requests that failed, by service
panels.description: Requests to staging and to the pull request previews that got a server error, by service. No customer is affected; a change that is about to be released may be broken.

panels.title: Error lines, by service, worker and database
panels.description: Lines written at error level on staging and the previews: by each service, each worker, and the database. Something failed there; the tables below show the app's own lines.

panels.title: Workers that stopped with an error
panels.description: Times a worker container on staging or a preview ended with an error code. A release or a scale-down is not counted. The jobs it was running start over.

panels.title: Newest error lines on staging
panels.description: The app's own lines at error level on staging, newest first. Fixed words only.

targets.queryText: severity>=ERROR AND (resource.type="cloud_run_revision" OR resource.type="cloud_run_worker_pool") AND (logName:"stdout" OR logName:"stderr") AND jsonPayload.message:*

panels.title: Newest error lines on the previews
panels.description: The app's own lines at error level on the pull request previews, newest first, with the number of the pull request.

targets.queryText: severity>=ERROR AND (resource.type="cloud_run_revision" OR resource.type="cloud_run_worker_pool") AND (logName:"stdout" OR logName:"stderr") AND jsonPayload.message:*

panels.title: sam in the selected time
panels.description: "sessions that broke" did not end the normal way (cut by a restart, ended in an error, got stuck or ran out of time; a cut one is counted 45 minutes after its last step): someone may still be waiting. "people with no reply" started a session that ended with no reply and no question back; some are answered by a later session in the same thread. "model calls that failed": sam tries again, many mean slow or missing answers. "age of the record" is how long ago sam's records were last copied into the database this row reads (every ten minutes); red from 30 minutes: this row is behind and can show zero while something fails.

targets.rawSql: select count(*) as "sessions that broke" from obs.sam_sessions where $__timeFilter(started_at) and exit_state <> 'clean'
select count(*) as "people with no reply" from obs.sam_sessions where $__timeFilter(started_at) and trigger = 'person' and not replied and exit_state <> 'cut'
select coalesce(sum(errors), 0) as "model calls that failed" from obs.minute_model_calls where $__timeFilter(minute)
select extract(epoch from now() - min(loaded_at)) as "age of the record" from obs.sam_loads where source in ('sessions', 'tool_calls', 'model_calls')

panels.title: Sessions that broke
panels.description: The sessions that broke, newest first: when it started, what started it, how it ended and how many steps it had taken. Empty: none broke.

targets.rawSql: select started_at as started, trigger as "started by", case exit_state when 'cut' then 'cut by a restart' when 'errored' then 'ended in an error' when 'stuck' then 'got stuck' when 'timed_out' then 'ran out of time' else exit_state end as "how it ended", tool_calls as steps, session_id as session from obs.sam_sessions where $__timeFilter(started_at) and exit_state <> 'clean' order by started_at desc limit 50

panels.title: Sessions that broke, by how
panels.description: Sessions that did not end the normal way, per hour, by how they ended. Bars after a release of sam are sessions that the restart cut.

targets.rawSql: select $__timeGroupAlias(started_at, 1h), case exit_state when 'cut' then 'cut by a restart' when 'errored' then 'ended in an error' when 'stuck' then 'got stuck' when 'timed_out' then 'ran out of time' else exit_state end as metric, count(*) as value from obs.sam_sessions where $__timeFilter(started_at) and exit_state <> 'clean' group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Steps that failed, by kind
panels.description: Steps sam took that failed in one of the known ways, per hour: a command with a mistake in it, a refused login, a query on a column that does not exist. sam tries another way; many of one kind make its answers slow and cost more.

targets.rawSql: select $__timeGroupAlias(ts, 1h), failure as metric, count(*) as value from obs.sam_tool_calls where $__timeFilter(ts) and failure is not null group by 1, 2 order by 1
